text:
jonas: Heads up — we're seeing a 2x P50 latency spike on qwen2.5-small in hosted-prod starting ~1712309600. Sudden KV cache miss/eviction rate increase on routes that handle mixed CJK+latin payloads. Any ideas? :eyes:

maria: Got the alert. Which route and can you share a short profile?

jonas: Route = /v1/generate:qwen2.5-small (zh+en customer). Quick profiler dump below — kernel selector flipped and evictions spiked around the time of the latency jump.

jonas: ```
PerfSampler: model=qwen2.5-small
  gpu_kernel: auto -> fallback_generic
  batcher: avg_batch_size 3 -> 9 (spike)
  kvcache: evictions/sec 0.2 -> 13.7
  chosen_kernel: matmul_bf16_unfused -> matmul_generic_fp32
  seq_len_dist: {short: 85%, long: 15%} (long sequences causing pad blowup)
```

adele: That looks like the selector switched to a safe generic kernel due to either a tensor-layout inference or dtype mismatch. Also suspicious: head vs kv_head mismatch can force a fallback. Did the tokenizer change for CJK?

jonas: We recently merged a small tokenizer tweak for multilang normalization (adds ZWJ in some edge cases). I reproduced locally — tokenizer sometimes splits CJK into smaller token units for mixed inputs which shifts kv indexing. Example: '你好world' can tokenize differently between versions (['你好','world'] vs ['你','好','world']).

sam: I think two things combine: 1) tokenization produces uneven sequence lengths in the batch which breaks our adaptive batch-slicer, making a few long sequences pad the whole batch; 2) that causes larger temporary KV allocations and then LRU eviction pressure. Kernel selector sees the larger shapes and chooses a more generic kernel.

sam: Reproducer command I used:
```bash
# repro script (local)
python tools/repro_batch_kv.py --model qwen2.5-small --inputs samples/mixed_cjk.json --batch-schedule adaptive --repeat 500
```

maria: I also noticed in the trace that the selector checks only "total_seq" and not "per_head / kv_head" dims — if kv_head != head dim (some Qwen variants have fused kv dims) selector heuristics misjudge memory layout. We should add an explicit kv_head dim check.

adele: Short mitigation: pin kernel to matmul_bf16_unfused for the affected canary route and clamp batcher max_seq_pad to 1024 for that route. I'll start a canary patch. Also adding a temporary rule: prefer splitting mixed-lang inputs into separate batches by language to avoid the pad blowup. :thumbsup:

runtime-bot: deploy started — canary: qwen2.5-route-zh pinned-kernel by adele at 1712310200.

jonas: Canary results after ~10 minutes: P50 back to baseline, evictions down to ~0.5/sec, kernel remained pinned. Looks promising. Need a proper root fix: tokenizer normalization + selector tunables + KV eviction weight by prefix hit frequency.

maria: I'll file RAL ticket with perf traces, repro steps, and suggested checklist: [1] add kv_head dim in selector, [2] add language-aware batch-splitting heuristic, [3] adjust KVCache LRU to consider prefix hits, [4] revert tokenizer ZWJ change until we vet.

adele: I'll write a short RFC for the selector heuristics (propose: explicit checks for kv_head/head mismatch, sequence-length skew threshold, and kernel fallback budget). Will cc eng-ml for tokenizer policy.

jonas: Thanks all. Keeping this thread for follow-ups. If anyone has microbenchmarks for matmul_bf16_unfused vs generic on these shapes please drop them here.

sam: dropping a quick perf note: local microbench matmul_bf16_unfused is ~2.7x faster on the common short-seq shapes we see, but only when kv layout matches expected strides.

maria: assigned to eng-runtime + eng-ml. Ticket RAL-512 created.

adele: will monitor canary for 2 hours and post final results. :eyes:
